_comment: SERVER-SIDE ONLY. Reveal stage 2 and 3 for Case A. Real, unscaled figures. USD millions.
basis_notes: Each quarter is shown as the company reported it at the time. Quarter 6 was reported after two units moved to discontinued operations, so its revenue is on a narrower basis than Quarters 4-5 (which still included cable installation revenue).
Quarter 3 comes from the annual report quarterly-data note; cash revenue and Adjusted EBITDA for it are secondary-sourced and flagged below.
All of 2000 and the first three quarters of 2001 were later restated (gc-10k-2002, Restatements).

From Quarter 3 the company reports 'Recurring Adjusted EBITDA', which excludes items it calls non-recurring; Quarters 1-2 in the play pack show 'Adjusted EBITDA'. The reveal labels the change so the line students cited still highlights.

text_lines.fact: $375m of cash revenue and Recurring Adjusted EBITDA came from significant carrier customers who signed contracts to buy $500m of capacity and to whom the company made substantial capital commitments in the same quarter; new capital commitments total about $625m
Shares received for the hosting unit fell from $1,918m at closing to $1,163m at 31 Mar 2001
text_lines.src: gc-10q-2001q1 p.6 note 5 (reveal only; names the Case B rival)

text_lines.fact: $345m of cash revenue and Recurring Adjusted EBITDA came from carriers who signed to buy $381m of capacity; the company made $358m of cash commitments to those carriers
Company expects slower growth from a lengthening sales cycle, customers' financial difficulties and an industry downturn; installation revenue expected to fall
Core network completed this quarter; capital spending guidance for the year cut to under $4,500m from $4,900-5,100m
Board approved eliminating more than 2,000 positions and a $250-325m charge
8.70% notes fair value $762 per $1,000 face (was $923 at 31 Mar)
Shares received for the hosting unit worth $223m vs $1,918m at closing
$152m of cash revenue came from carriers who signed to buy $177m of capacity; company cash commitments to those carriers $190m in the quarter ($1,173m over three quarters)
Company expects to need modifications to financial covenants to stay in compliance
Credit ratings cut in October; receivables facility and a $61m borrowing called
Complete evaluation of long-lived assets in the next quarter may bring a material write-down of goodwill
Carrier revenue flat; many providers deferred capacity purchases; carrier data customers delayed renewals
More than 2,000 jobs cut, a further ~1,200 planned; headcount to fall below 8,000

outcome.fact: Filed for Chapter 11 on 28 January 2002, listing about $22.4bn of assets and $12.4bn of debt. Common and preferred shareholders were wiped out.
outcome.src: Chapter 11 petition, 28 Jan 2002, as summarised in House Financial Services Committee memo (21 Mar 2002) https://financialservices.house.gov/media/pdf/032102wm.pdf
outcome.open_item: Confirm against the company 8-K of 28 Jan 2002

outcome.fact: The SEC later found that the company described reciprocal capacity purchases and sales in its reports without saying how much of its cash revenue and Adjusted EBITDA depended on them; the company and executives consented to a cease-and-desist order.
outcome.open_item: Wording confirmed against order for the figures below; keep student-facing text to what the order states

outcome.fact: The SEC order states that in the quarter to March 2001, reciprocal deals made up 23% of cash revenue and 85% of Recurring Adjusted EBITDA. In the quarter to June 2001, without them, the reported $472m would have been about minus $43m.
A board special committee later reviewed 16 of 36 concurrent purchase-and-sale deals made between October 2000 and September 2001.
The company restated 2000 and the first three quarters of 2001.
The network kept running through bankruptcy; a new owner put in fresh equity at emergence and the business was later bought by another network operator.
